one_line: Founder-sultan who unified Bengal’s riverine provinces into a single Sultanate in the mid-14th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, medium height, solid and athletic build with a commander’s bearing.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium-brown Bengal delta complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, intense almond-shaped eyes with a calm, strategic gaze, default expression composed and authoritative with a hint of stern focus.
appearance.hair: Black hair kept short and tidy under a tall conical quilted turban in deep indigo, wrapped with a narrow white cloth band and a small metal turban ornament at the forehead.
appearance.costume: Fourteenth-century Bengal Sultanate martial court attire: a long quilted cotton jama (coat) in deep indigo blue reaching just below the knees, front-opening with a row of simple bronze toggles and a slightly flared skirt; beneath it, hints of a light cream cotton tunic at collar and cuffs; a wide dark red leather kamarband (belt) wrapped twice at the waist, with one end tucked and another hanging neatly; straight, slightly loose trousers in muted olive green, tucked into mid-calf height brown leather riding boots; over the torso, a fitted lamellar cuirass of small iron plates laced together over a padded base, dark metallic with subtle wear; forearms protected by simple iron bracers strapped over the jama sleeves; minimal but dignified jewellery—small gold hoop in one ear and a plain signet ring on the right hand—evoking courtly status without ostentation.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved single-edged Indo-Persian style sword (early tulwar form) with a simple iron cross-guard, a dark wood hilt bound with red leather, and a scabbard in deep indigo with plain bronze fittings, worn at his left hip and often held lightly in his right hand in a ready-but-disciplined stance.

ref_desc: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah has a medium-brown oval face with short beard, an indigo conical turban, a deep indigo quilted jama over lamellar armor, olive trousers, brown boots, a dark red belt, and carries a curved Indo-Persian sword in an indigo scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah as a dignified 14th-century Bengal sultan and commander: a medium-height, athletic man in his late thirties with a medium-brown oval face, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short black beard and moustache, and intense almond-shaped eyes set in a calm, authoritative expression. His black hair is short and mostly hidden by a tall conical quilted turban in deep indigo, wrapped with a narrow white band and a small metal ornament at the forehead. He wears a long deep indigo quilted cotton jama that opens at the front with bronze toggles and flares slightly below the knees, showing a light cream tunic at the collar and cuffs. Over his torso is a fitted lamellar iron cuirass, dark metallic and slightly worn, with simple iron bracers on his forearms. A wide dark red leather belt is wrapped firmly at his waist, and straight olive green trousers are tucked into sturdy mid-calf brown leather riding boots. Minimal jewellery—a small gold hoop earring and a plain ring—signal status without excess. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon: a slightly curved single-edged Indo-Persian style sword with an iron cross-guard, a dark wood hilt bound in red leather, and a deep indigo scabbard with bronze fittings, which he holds lightly in one hand in a poised, disciplined manner. Show him from head to toe, emphasizing the indigo and dark red palette, the realistic armor and garments, and his composed, strategic presence suitable for consistent redraws across panels.
